Stand down on new credit spreads today, or push DTE past the election/payrolls window and cut size hard.

focus.jbig: Midterm election day · oil rebounds on US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island · VIX back above 21 · AI correction · 6 setups boarded
focus.jtag: Crude bounced ~1–2% after a reported US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island reversed Monday’s ~7% peace-hope plunge; the VIX popped back above 21 as Apple’s margin warning hit tech and the Nasdaq-100 sat in correction. The scanner boarded CLX & FANG (Type A, bullish) plus MO, MA, LLY and XLP (Type C, bullish breakouts)
focus.jnote: The backdrop is a two-sided event cluster, not an all-clear. The S&P 500 dropped 38.67 points, or 0.51%, to 7,541.40 on Monday as the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4%, entering correction territory, while the Dow rose 0.4% on questions about AI-investment returns. This morning the tape is split: Dow futures fell ~0.8% and S&P futures were roughly flat, while Nasdaq-100 futures ticked higher after a turbulent day for chip stocks. The big overnight mover is crude — WTI rose ~1.8% to ~$98 and Brent ~2% to ~$107 after a reported US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz revived supply-disruption fears, reversing Monday’s plunge when Brent settled down 7.63% at $104.77 on peace hopes. Vol is bid again: the VIX rose 8.91% to ~21.15 after October’s stress in crowded technology trades, driven in part by Apple and Palantir selling off premarket on margin and valuation concerns. And the calendar is loaded: markets focused on the US midterm elections, employment data, and corporate earnings, with AMD reporting after the close. Calmer than a live war, but not the quiet tape a Sniper wants to sell premium into.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded bullish names, the held breakouts (MO, MA, LLY) are the cleanest technically, and the two Type A gaps (CLX, FANG) report earnings behind them. MO (Altria) is a low-beta tobacco staple holding above its $76.07 pivot on ~1.6x volume — the best defensive fit for a jittery tape. Clorox beat revenue estimates with sales up 33.3% to $1.91 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.55, 44.6% above consensus, a genuine double-beat. FANG (Diamondback) also reported strong Q3 results including $5.43 billion in revenue, $2.1 billion in free cash flow, and higher 2026 oil-production guidance. But on a RED day with the VIX near 21, midterm results landing overnight and AMD after the close, every one is watch-only — young breakouts and light-volume gaps fail easily when election and earnings headlines whip the tape.
focus.notup: No bearish single-name boarded today. Type B produced zero gap-confirmed catalysts; the dominant stories — the oil rebound on the Qeshm strike, the AI-capex correction, and midterm positioning — are macro/market moves, not clean named in-universe Type B catalysts. Selling a bear call into a VIX-rising, election-day tape invites a violent squeeze on any relief or de-escalation headline. Sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? P(≥1% gap) at ~42% is above the 35% trigger — that alone locks out GREEN — and composite ~61 sits in WARM. The oil rebound re-arms the geopolitical tail just as the midterm elections, AMD’s print tonight, JOLTS at 10:00, and Friday’s payrolls stack unscheduled-outcome catalysts in a row, with the Nasdaq-100 already in a 10%+ correction. Every boarded Type A name printed on near-zero relative volume and every Type C is a 0–2-session-old breakout. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the event cluster and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Boarded Type C, graded A+, bullish — the top name on the board: a held breakout in a low-beta defensive, exactly the profile for a jittery election-day tape. Altria broke to a new 52-week high (zone ~$79.81) and the breakout has now HELD 2 sessions above its $76.07 pivot (price ~$76.52, extended just ~0.6%), stronger than a same-day pop. Breakout-day volume ran ~1.59x the 50-day average, clearing the 1.3x bar, and a tobacco staple with a steady dividend tends to hold up when risk assets wobble. 3 S/R layers sit within 7% (pivot $76.07, sma20 $73.57, swing $71.56). Liquidity passed: ATM spread $0.36 (bar $0.39), OI 751 on the Nov-20 $77 chain. Next earnings ~Feb 4, 2027 — well outside any normal DTE. Still watch-only on a RED day.

If taken later, confirm at 9:35 that price > the $76.07 pivot AND > open AND holding the upper third of range; half size. Liquidity verified by the scanner — still re-check at the open.

scenarios.label: Most likely — Headline whipsaw into the election count
scenarios.sub: The tape lurches on each Iran/oil and AI-earnings headline while traders de-risk ahead of overnight midterm results, JOLTS and AMD; choppy, no clean trend, VIX stays bid near 21

scenarios.label: Bad case — AI rout resumes / AMD or results shock
scenarios.sub: AMD disappoints after the close, the AI-capex derate re-cracks tech, or a blue-sweep election read pressures AI stocks; the Nasdaq extends its correction and the VIX pushes toward the mid-20s

scenarios.label: Good case — Relief rally
scenarios.sub: A clean Iran de-escalation headline plus a benign election outcome and solid AMD print let oil fade and the oversold Nasdaq bounce; the VIX eases back toward 17–18

scenarios.label: Tail — Hormuz shock / contested election
scenarios.sub: A Strait of Hormuz incident spikes crude back toward $110+, or a contested/uncertain election outcome triggers a sharp VIX blow-off across risk assets

risks: Midterm elections today — poll closing times vary by state, with the earliest major-state counts (Florida, Georgia, Virginia) beginning at midnight GMT. An uncertain, contested, or blue-sweep outcome is an unscheduled overnight gap catalyst — the number-one thing to watch tonight.

AMD after the close & the AI correction — AMD reports after the close with the market hypersensitive to AI reads after Apple’s margin warning, and the Nasdaq-100 has already dropped into correction territory. A soft guide can re-crack the whole index overnight.

US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island & Hormuz — a reported US strike on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, described as defensive, revived supply-disruption fears, and markets stay volatile between renewed diplomacy and the risk of further military escalation. Any shipping disruption sends crude vertical.

Oil & a possible December rate hike — rebounding crude feeds inflation fear, and futures markets place the probability of an additional December increase near 75%, though Monday’s oil drop eased some immediate inflation risk. A rate pop compounds pressure on stocks.

JOLTS today (10:00) & payrolls Friday — the labor-data cluster can whip rates and risk; weaker payrolls could ease tightening expectations while resilient employment and sticky inflation would reinforce higher-for-longer. A scheduled event any 7-DTE spread must clear.
